primary_diagnosis: Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD) with Recurrent Acid Peptic Disease
clinical_reasoning: Patient with a history of responsive acid peptic disease presents with breakthrough epigastric and retrosternal burning and pain despite self-resuming prior acid-suppressing medication. While excessive gas symptoms responded to treatment, refractory mucosal burning indicates ongoing gastric hyperacidity or subacute mucosal irritation characteristic of GERD / recurrent gastritis.
recommended_tests: Helicobacter pylori Stool Antigen Test or Urea Breath Test
Trial of optimized Proton Pump Inhibitor (PPI) and mucosal protectant therapy
